titre_page: How do I animate a character from a single picture? | Yop2D guide
description: In Yop2D, load a single character picture, place a skeleton, outline its parts and get the Idle, Walk, Run, Jump, Attack and Hit animations without drawing anything else.
h1: How do I animate a character from a single picture?
carte: One picture is enough: Yop2D makes the walk, the jump, the attack…
etapes: Assets window → "Character" button, then choose your picture.
Drag each circle onto a joint, then outline each part.
With the stamp, the color or the fill, repair what shows when an arm moves.
Choose the movements and tap "Create the pictures".
blocs: You have **a single picture** of your character, seen from the side? Yop2D cuts it into pieces (head, arms, legs…) and moves them to make the **Idle, Walk, Run, Jump, Attack and Hit** animations. You don't have to draw anything else, and you don't need to prepare a sprite sheet.
a project open in the editor;
a picture of your character seen from the side, preferably on a transparent background (feet on the ground, arms and legs clearly visible).
At the top, tap the **Character** button, then **Choose the character picture**.
The character must face **right** to work. If it faces left, tap **Flip the picture (mirror)**: your final pictures will still face left.
The **↶** and **↷** buttons at the top undo and redo almost everything (up to 60 actions): try freely.
Tap **Place the skeleton for me**: Yop2D tries to guess where the joints are.
Then fix it: drag each circle onto the real joint (neck, shoulder, elbow, hand, hip, knees, ankles, toes). A magnifier shows the spot under your finger.
Tap a circle to read, under its name, where it should go.
Put the circles on the **axis** of the joint (the point the arm or leg turns around), not on its edge. The more accurate they are, the nicer the movement.
Tap the **Outlines** step, then a part in the list or directly on the picture.
Drag its points to follow the drawing's outline. A small **+** in the middle of a side adds a point; **Remove the chosen point** removes one.
For an outline that is already well placed, try **Automatic outline**.
Arms and legs are cut into several pieces (arm and forearm, thigh, shin and foot): that is what lets the elbow and knee bend.

When an arm or a leg moves, it leaves a gap where it was. The **Stamp** step shows the character in motion so you can see those gaps. Always start with **1. Pick the source area**: tap a clean spot of the drawing, for example the clothing.
**2. Paint over the hole:** Yop2D copies the chosen area onto the hole, like a stamp.
**2b. Paint with the area's color:** the brush paints with one flat color, the one of the chosen area. Handy for a tear.
**2c. Fill by placing points:** place points all around the hole, then tap **Fill the area**. You can move a point before lifting your finger.
**3. Eraser (remove hanging bits):** erases what sticks out or hangs. The slider sets the size of the brush and the eraser.
**Undo last stroke** and **Clear all** let you start over.
If the color spills over, go over it with the eraser: you can always fix it.
Step 5: choose the movement and try it
In the **Animate** step, choose a movement: Idle, Walk, Run, Jump, Attack or Hit. You see it moving in a loop.
Set the **speed** (frames per second) and the **movement size** (for smaller or bigger steps).
In the **Create** step, give your character a name and tick the movements to make.
Tap **Create the pictures**. They are saved in your project's Images folder, and the animations are added to the list.

To use them, place your character in the scene and give it the "platformer character" behavior: it recognizes the idle, walk, run and jump animations by itself. You can also play them with [[jouer_animation]].
The animation names (idle, walk, jump…) are the ones Yop2D's behaviors recognize: you have nothing to set.
**The character faces the wrong way:** tap "Flip the picture (mirror)" in step 1.
**A limb has a gap when it moves:** go to the Stamp step and fill it (source area, color or fill).
**You see two arms:** untick "This part stays on the body" in the list of parts.
**The result looks damaged:** use ↶ to go back, or place the skeleton points more precisely.
**The drawing is seen from the front:** for now, the workshop works on a character seen from the side.
